column3: Close to the Hebrew; יִרְאָתְךָ (“fear [of God]”) is rendered “reverence.”
Close to the Hebrew; the lion terms are rendered “The old lion” and “the cubs of the lioness.”
NKJV renders וְרוּחַ (“wind, spirit”) as “a spirit.”
NKJV renders דְּמָמָה (“a whisper, silence”) as “There was silence,” and supplies “saying.”
NKJV takes “from God” as comparative, “more righteous than God,” rather than “righteous before God.”
Close to the Hebrew; וּבְמַלְאָכָיו (“his messengers”) is rendered “His angels.”
Close to the Hebrew; “with no one setting [heart]” is rendered “with no one regarding.”
NKJV renders יִתְרָם (“their tent cord”) as “their own excellence,” following a different sense of the word.
